lines.text: Every universe keeps its own time. Its own heroes. Its own endings.

lines.speaker: OMOLOLU (V.O.)
lines.text: Mine kept me. A normal kid. A normal room. A normal Tuesday.

lines.speaker: OMOLOLU
lines.text: ...okay, that's the third time the lights flickered. Totally normal. Not ominous at all.

lines.speaker: OMOLOLU
lines.text: Wait. Why is the AIR opening?
The room folds inward. A seam of white light tears the world open — and swallows him whole.

lines.speaker: RICK PRIME
lines.text: There he goes. Right on schedule.

lines.speaker: RICK PRIME
lines.text: Every anchor thinks the fracture chose them. None of them like the real answer.
ACT I  —  THE NEXUS FRACTURE
He wakes where all worlds bleed together: the Nexus. A bruise-colored sky over ground that remembers a hundred battlefields.

lines.speaker: OMOLOLU
lines.text: Where... am I? This is definitely not Tuesday.

lines.speaker: OMOLOLU
lines.text: Two of them. Already fighting. Great first impression, universe.

lines.speaker: GENOS
lines.text: Identify yourself. This sector is unstable — and you are standing in it.

lines.speaker: ICHIGO
lines.text: He's not the problem, tin man. Stand down and I'll explain.

lines.speaker: GENOS
lines.text: Negotiation is inefficient.

lines.speaker: ICHIGO
lines.text: You done venting? Good. Now LISTEN.

lines.speaker: GENOS
lines.text: ...Threat reassessed. You are not hostile. Logged.
The Nexus mimics whatever it devours. A whole aisle of a corner store hums under dead fluorescent light in the middle of nowhere.

lines.speaker: OMOLOLU
lines.text: A grocery store. In the void. With snacks. I'm either dreaming or dead — either way I'm starving.

lines.speaker: ICHIGO
lines.text: Don't eat the void food, kid. Come on — there's a fire, and people who aren't trying to kill you. Mostly.
A man in a spiral mask waits at the edge of the light. He does not blink. He does not need to.

lines.speaker: OBITO
lines.text: The new anchor. Small. Frightened. Perfect.

lines.speaker: OMOLOLU
lines.text: Anchor? Man, I don't even have a driver's license.

lines.speaker: OBITO
lines.text: Then let me measure exactly what you're worth to the fracture.

lines.speaker: OMOLOLU
lines.text: Okay. OKAY. I did a thing. A violent thing. And it WORKED.

lines.speaker: OBITO
lines.text: ...You'll do. That was never a fight, boy. It was a measurement — and he was watching.
Night, if the Nexus keeps nights. A campfire snaps. Strangers from a dozen dead worlds share its light.

lines.speaker: ICHIGO
lines.text: You held your own against a masked freak on day one. That buys you a seat at the fire.

lines.speaker: OMOLOLU
lines.text: So what IS this place? And why does everyone keep calling me an anchor?
No one answers right away. The fire pops. Somewhere past the light, Rick Prime is already writing the next chapter.
END OF ACT I
ACT II  —  THE SHRINKING GROUND
The Nexus is smaller today. Yesterday's horizon is this morning's wall. Whole dead worlds fold shut like books no one will reopen.

lines.speaker: OMOLOLU
lines.text: The ground keeps... ending. Every night there's less of it. Less of us.

lines.speaker: GENOS
lines.text: The fracture is contracting toward a single point. My sensors put us inside its collapse radius. We do not have long.
Where the strongest gather, the ground lasts longest — so the strongest come to fight over what's left. Two of them are already here.

lines.speaker: GOJO
lines.text: Only one cursed king gets to hold this piece of the world, and it isn't going to be you.

lines.speaker: SUKUNA
lines.text: Then stand in my domain and be measured, sorcerer. I have been bored for a thousand years.

lines.speaker: GOJO
lines.text: Throughout heaven and earth... yeah. You know the rest.
The killing blow never lands. A spear of cursed steel splits the air between them — and the man who fears nothing steps out of the dark.

lines.speaker: TOJI
lines.text: Sorcerers. Kings. Same soft throat under all the talk. I'll take the ground — and the bounty on both your heads.

lines.speaker: TOJI
lines.text: No cursed energy. No tricks. Just a man who's better at this than you. Remember that.
Elsewhere, four powers that could each end the others meet on the last wide plain. Nobody moves. Everybody is doing the math.

lines.speaker: BEERUS
lines.text: A god of destruction, and... whatever you are. You don't even register to me. That's either an insult or a miracle.

lines.speaker: VEGETA
lines.text: Frieza. Of every ruin the multiverse could spit back at me, it had to be you. Good. I still owe you a death.

lines.speaker: VEGETA
lines.text: That's twice now. Stay down this time — you're embarrassing us both.

lines.speaker: SAITAMA
lines.text: So you're a god, huh. Cool. I was gonna ask if the sale's still on, but... okay. One punch first.

lines.speaker: BEERUS
lines.text: ...What ARE you. No mortal — no GOD — hits like that. Whis is going to have questions.
Under the last intact roof in the Nexus, the survivors call a council. Heroes, monsters, gods — one table, one shrinking world.

lines.speaker: ICHIGO
lines.text: Everyone here has killed someone everyone else here loved. And we still have to pick a plan by morning.

lines.speaker: OMOLOLU
lines.text: So the anchor gets a vote now? Yesterday nobody would even tell me what an anchor is.

lines.speaker: GENOS
lines.text: You ARE the vote. Every collapse curves toward you. Wherever you stand, the ground holds a little longer. That is what an anchor is.
Beyond the firelight, something older than any world at the table watches the council decide. It has watched a thousand councils. None of them mattered.

lines.speaker: RICK PRIME
lines.text: Cute. They think choosing together makes the choice theirs. Every anchor's little parliament ends the exact same way.

lines.speaker: RICK PRIME
lines.text: I don't have to break their alliance. I just have to be there when it breaks itself.
One face at the fire keeps finding yours across the flames. Not an enemy. Worse — a measure. The one you'd have to beat to matter here.

lines.speaker: ICHIGO
lines.text: You've got the anchor's luck, kid, but luck isn't a spine. When the ground finally comes for us, I need to know you won't run.

lines.speaker: OMOLOLU
lines.text: I didn't run from the masked man. I'm not running from you. When it comes — I'll be on the last piece of ground there is.
The alliance doesn't break itself. It's broken — from the dark, all at once. Three shapes drop through the collapsing sky with a plan and a list of names.

lines.speaker: RICK PRIME
lines.text: There it is — the moment a parliament becomes a panic. Take the anchor last. I want it to watch its friends go first.

lines.speaker: DEATHSTROKE
lines.text: Contract's simple, machine. Everyone here stops working. Starting with the one that never sleeps.

lines.speaker: GENOS
lines.text: Contract terminated. Threat two — reacquiring.

lines.speaker: FRIEZA
lines.text: A soul reaper. How quaint. I have unmade emperors, boy. Let me add a shinigami to the list.

lines.speaker: ICHIGO
lines.text: You talk like every villain I've ever buried. Get in line.
Two of the three are down. And the oldest, coldest one hasn't moved — because it was only ever here for one of them.

lines.speaker: RICK PRIME
lines.text: Just you and me now, anchor. No masked measurer. No tin man. Let's find out what the fracture actually built.

lines.speaker: OMOLOLU
lines.text: You've been in every shadow since my bedroom wall opened. Fine. Come find out. I'm done being measured.

lines.speaker: OMOLOLU
lines.text: That's for the bedroom. And the Tuesday. And every single 'right on schedule.'

lines.speaker: RICK PRIME
lines.text: ...Good. GOOD. You hit like something worth collapsing a multiverse to catch. NOW you're worth the real conversation.
Three attackers driven off. The ground you saved is smaller than the ground you lost saving it. This is what winning costs in the Nexus now.

lines.speaker: OMOLOLU
lines.text: We won. So why does it feel like he LET us? Like the whole ambush was just... one more measurement.

lines.speaker: ICHIGO
lines.text: Because it was. Rest while you can, anchor. Whatever he's really building — next time he won't be watching. He'll be finishing it.
END OF ACT II
ACT III  —  THE CONVERGENCE
There is a word for it in a language the Nexus never learned: Ìlẹ̀kùn. A door. The fracture was never a wound. It was a threshold — and it has been waiting for someone to open it.

lines.speaker: OMOLOLU
lines.text: My grandmother used to say a door only opens for the one holding the key. I never asked what happens to the key after.

lines.speaker: GENOS
lines.text: The collapse has a center now, and the center is a door. Rick Prime doesn't want to close the fracture. He wants to walk THROUGH it — and he needs the anchor to hold it open.
The Nexus splits one last time — not the ground this time, but the people standing on it. Every survivor has to decide what the last door is worth.

lines.speaker: ICHIGO
lines.text: Some of them are already walking toward him. Power calls to power, and he's the loudest thing in any world now. So I'll ask once: where do you stand, anchor?

lines.speaker: OMOLOLU
lines.text: On the threshold. Between him and the door. If he wants through, he goes through me first. That's where I stand.

lines.speaker: GOJO
lines.text: Good answer. Then the strongest of every world hold the line while you hold the door. Try not to die — I only just started finding you interesting.
And then every world arrives at once. The convergence. A hundred legends on one collapsing field, and the only rule left is: keep the line until the anchor seals the door.

lines.speaker: VEGETA
lines.text: You crawled out of one more grave, Frieza. Allow me to dig the last one myself.
— CUT. Across the field, a cursed king meets two sorcerers who fight as one. —
— CUT. In the ruins of a borrowed Gotham, the mercenary meets the one man who plans faster than he does. —
— CUT. A mountain of gathered stone falls from the sky. A god of destruction simply... disagrees with it. —
— CUT. A ninja and the masked man who broke the world fight side by side against the ghost who taught them both. —
— CUT. Two strongest-men-alive stand back to back against an emperor's endless army. —
— CUT. And a bald man in a yellow suit walks up to a god who erases timelines, sighs, and raises one fist. —

lines.speaker: SAITAMA
lines.text: Huh. Was that supposed to be the strong one? ...Anyone know if the sale's still on?
The line holds. Impossibly, gloriously, the line holds — every world buying the anchor the seconds it needs. Which leaves exactly one door, and one man walking calmly toward it.

lines.speaker: RICK PRIME
lines.text: Everyone else is a distraction I arranged. You were always the only variable. Step aside from the door, anchor — or become the last thing the fracture ever measures.

lines.speaker: OMOLOLU
lines.text: You collapsed a multiverse to build a key. Congratulations. The key says no.
Everything the Nexus has left narrows to this: a boy who was nobody, and the oldest, coldest thing in creation, on the last piece of ground, in front of the last open door.

lines.speaker: OMOLOLU
lines.text: You spent forever looking for the one anchor that could hold the door. You found him. You just didn't think he'd hold it shut.

lines.speaker: RICK PRIME
lines.text: ...Every version of this. Every timeline. And it ends with a kid and a locked door. ...Fine. Seal it. Let's see if you can live with what that costs, too.

The anchor holds. The door begins to close — and as it closes, it un-fractures: every borrowed world sliding back toward the timeline it was torn from. The Nexus is ending the only kind way it can. By sending everyone home.

lines.speaker: ICHIGO
lines.text: So this is it. The seams close, we all wake up where we started, and nobody back home believes a word of it. You did good, kid. Better than good.

lines.speaker: GOJO
lines.text: You held a door against the end of everything. Wherever you land — don't let them tell you you're normal. I'll know they're lying.

lines.speaker: OMOLOLU
lines.text: Will I remember? Any of you? Or does the door take that too?
No one answers. The light folds gently inward — not a tear this time, but a closing hand — and one by one, a hundred legends wink back into the worlds that need them. Last of all, the anchor.
END OF ACT III
EPILOGUE
A normal room. A normal bed. A normal Tuesday, exactly where he left it — as if the air never opened at all.

lines.speaker: OMOLOLU
lines.text: ...A dream. Obviously. Grocery stores in the void. A bald guy who ends gods. A door. Obviously a dream.

lines.speaker: OMOLOLU
lines.text: So why do my knuckles still hurt. And why do I miss people I've apparently never met.

He almost believes it. He almost lets it go. And then he looks up — and there, running the length of his perfectly normal ceiling, is a hairline crack that was never there before. Faint. Patient. Widening by a single thread.

lines.speaker: OMOLOLU
lines.text: ...Okay. Not a dream.
— POST-CREDITS —
Somewhere with no world attached to it — a place between the closed door and the next one — a single figure sits in the dark, unhurried, already working.

lines.speaker: RICK PRIME
lines.text: One anchor closed one door. There are others. There are always others.

lines.speaker: RICK PRIME
lines.text: And now I know exactly what the right one is worth. ...Right on schedule.
THE NEXUS FRACTURE  —  to be continued
